result:
Windows now have a "Keep on top" pin, and the JS checks CI runs (lint, typecheck, full vitest) all pass. Nothing is committed: you're on a detached HEAD and didn't ask for a commit.

There's no contributor guide in this checkout; the latest commits removed `docs/`, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. So I treated the JavaScript checks CI runs as the workflow.

**What I changed**
- **Stacking** (`src/window-manager/index.ts`): the window manager's stack still tracks focus order. When it sets z-indexes, kept-on-top windows go above all the others. So if you focus or open a normal window, it gets focus but stays drawn underneath. Several kept-on-top windows stack among themselves in focus order. A child window of a kept-on-top window is lifted with it, so it never ends up hidden behind its owner.
- **API**: `windowManager.setAlwaysOnTop( windowId, enabled )` returns `true` if something changed. Each window has a read-only `alwaysOnTop` property and a `toggleAlwaysOnTop()` method. A change fires `os-window-changed` with reason `'always-on-top'`, which also triggers the session save.
- **Pin button**: a new built-in title-bar control, `core/always-on-top`, uses a new `pin` icon. It shows as pressed when on and stays correct when the title bar is redrawn. I placed it just before minimize (`order: 8`) rather than first, because plugins use `order: 5` to put their own buttons at the start. There's also a CSS variable so window themes can reorder or hide it, like the other buttons.
- **Survives reload**: the session saves `alwaysOnTop: true` and restores it for both normal and native windows. The server-side session sanitizer (`includes/session.php`) only keeps known keys, so I added the new one there; without that it would be dropped on save.

**Checks I ran**
- `npm run lint`: no errors. The 16 warnings are all the file-length rule, and I didn't add any errors.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `npm run test:js`: 532 test files passed, 1 skipped. That includes a new `tests/vitest/window-always-on-top.test.ts` covering stacking, focus, child windows, the pin button, session save and restore.
- `npm run lint:css:unused`: clean.
- I updated `tests/vitest/window-chrome-controls-render.test.ts`, which listed the exact set of built-in buttons.
- As asked, I didn't start Docker or wp-env or run the PHP tests, so the PHP change was only syntax-checked with `php -l`.

**Limits to know about**
- A fullscreen window still covers kept-on-top windows, because fullscreen has its own higher layer.
- The setting only applies on the workspace the window belongs to.
- Saved workspace layouts don't record it; only the session does.
- Desktop themes can't supply a custom pin icon yet. That would need a new theme slot on both the JavaScript and PHP side.
